plugins.name: openspec
plugins.description: Personal engineering standard: OpenSpec (proposal/specs/design/tasks) with unattended implementation via the `auto` skill, rare ADRs written only at archive time, and Mermaid architecture diagrams kept current as part of each change. Run the `init` skill (user-only) in a new or existing project to apply it.
plugins.manifestDescription: Personal engineering standard: OpenSpec (proposal/specs/design/tasks) with unattended implementation via the `auto` skill, rare ADRs written only at archive time, and Mermaid architecture diagrams kept current as part of each change. Run the `init` skill (user-only) in a new or existing project to apply it.

skills.name: adr
skills.description: Record one Architecture Decision Record under docs/adr/ when the user asks for it, or to backfill a past decision that predates this project's docs/adr/ convention. ADRs in the normal flow are written at archive time, not here - this skill is the out-of-band path, not a second routine door. Requires the project to have already run the `init` skill (docs/adr/ must exist).

skills.name: auto
skills.description: Work an OpenSpec change's tasks.md to completion without stopping for approval - deciding alone when the plan runs out, recording each decision for review afterwards, and interrupting only on a closed list of conditions. Use when a change should be implemented unattended - "implementa sozinho", "vai até o fim", "não me pergunta", an overnight run, a long task list nobody is watching. Requires a project that ran the `init` skill and a change with a tasks.md.

skills.name: init
skills.description: Apply the personal engineering standard to this project - OpenSpec (with ADRs formalized at archive time) + Mermaid architecture diagrams. Works on a new (empty/near-empty) or an existing project. Deliberate, one-time bootstrap: human-invoked only; not meant to be auto-discovered by the model.

plugins.name: git
plugins.description: Personal git workflow conventions: a Conventional Commits skill and a pull/merge request skill (gitflow branches, conventional titles).
plugins.manifestDescription: Personal git workflow conventions: Conventional Commits and gitflow-named pull/merge requests.

skills.name: commit
skills.description: Commit (and push) changes using Conventional Commits. Use this whenever the user explicitly asks to commit, push, save, or check in changes - "commit this", "commit and push", "save my work", "git commit", "faz um commit" - and also proactively, on your own initiative, once a unit of work is genuinely done, not only when explicitly asked. Applies in any project with a git repository.

skills.name: pr
skills.description: Open, name and describe a pull/merge request (GitHub PR, GitLab MR) and its branch. Use whenever the user asks to open a PR/MR, "abre um PR", "cria o MR", "manda pra revisão", or when finished work on a branch needs to reach the default branch through review - and before publishing a branch for review, to name it right. Applies in any project with a remote and a review flow.

plugins.name: tui
plugins.description: Terminal UI media - starting with a record skill that generates a demo video from a spec: one file says what the video shows and how to rebuild the sandbox it was recorded in.
plugins.manifestDescription: Terminal UI media: recording a TUI as a demo video people will actually watch — isolated, verified, reproducible.

skills.name: record
skills.description: Record a terminal UI as a demo video worth publishing - an asciinema cast driven by a scripted, verified take, then cut and rendered to a GIF. Use whenever someone asks to record, film, capture or demo a TUI or CLI; to produce a README hero, a docs landing animation, a release-notes clip or a bug repro; or to redo a recording that is too long, too slow, robotic, visually off, or that leaked personal data. Also use when a recording driver misclicks, a beat silently does nothing, a long-running operation inside the app makes the video wait, or a rendered GIF comes out blank, padded in the wrong colour, or too heavy to embed. Not for editing existing video files, screen-recording a GUI, or writing docs prose to accompany a demo.
skills.compatibility: bash, tmux, asciinema (2.x or 3.x) and python3 for recording and cutting; agg for GIF rendering; ffmpeg optional, for inspecting frames and for mp4.

plugins.name: env
plugins.description: Machine and environment management through dotfiles: a machine is a build product of its chezmoi source directory, so installing a tool or changing a config means writing it there and applying, never by hand. Reads the setup's own lanes and conventions instead of assuming a package manager, and answers "is it in sync?" on all four axes - machine, source, remote, and what was never provisioned at all.
plugins.manifestDescription: The machine as a build product of its dotfiles: nothing is installed or configured by hand, everything goes through the chezmoi source and is applied from it.

skills.name: sync
skills.description: Keep a machine and its dotfiles repo the same thing - install and configure through the dotfiles source directory, never by hand. Use whenever someone asks to install or set up anything on their machine (a CLI, a package, a runtime, a font, a desktop app - "instala o X", "poe o Y na maquina", "set this up"), whenever a config file in the home directory needs changing, and whenever they ask whether the environment is in sync, what drifted, or why a fresh machine would not come out the same. Also use right after something was installed by hand, to write it back before it is forgotten. Machine-scoped - applies in any project, or in none.
skills.compatibility: chezmoi 2.x with its source directory under version control. Any platform chezmoi runs on - the package managers, script names and numbering are read from the source directory being managed, never assumed by this skill.
